clue.text: Fit, as expected, sporting my 'sox'

parts.note: something that is par for the course is just as expected

indicators.note: the letters are worn in a new arrangement, as if sporting them like clothing

explanation.surface: Someone throws a fit over socks they are expected to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' looks like a verb about clothes; it is a sudden attack. Quote marks around 'sox' are only surface dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden violent attack of emotion or illness is a fit.

clue.text: Place from which to steer sanctimonious group home

parts.note: pi is crossword slang for pious or sanctimonious
a lot is a group or batch
a house is a home

explanation.surface: A self-righteous bunch heads back to their dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The cabin on a boat holding the wheel is where the helmsman steers from.

clue.text: Rues timeless Holy City's backsliding

indicators.note: the word for rues loses T, the abbreviation for time

parts.note: to rue something is to regret it
Sion (Zion) is a name for Jerusalem, the Holy City

explanation.surface: Someone laments Jerusalem slipping back from its former state.
explanation.definitionFit: Relapse into an earlier, worse state is backsliding.

clue.text: Fibrous plant tissue found in waxy lemons

indicators.note: the answer is concealed within the run of letters of the next words

explanation.surface: A botanist notes the woody fibres inside waxed citrus fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Woody vascular tissue conducting water in plants is the botanical term defined.

clue.text: Son is gloomiest when upset — he'll predict earth-shattering events

indicators.note: upset means the letters are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A son is at his gloomiest when upset, while a scientist forecasts disasters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when upset' shuffles IS GLOOMIEST into EISMOLOGIST after S. 'Earth-shattering' looks figurative but literally means earthquakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who studies earthquakes tries to forecast tremors.

clue.text: Fruit, very soft, put into drinks

indicators.note: the musical marking is placed inside the word for drinks

parts.note: ales are drinks
pp (pianissimo) is the musical marking for very soft

explanation.surface: Soft fruit is added to drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchard produce such as Coxes is a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Elephant possibly getting cramp perambulating round park

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the name of the park
walking about suggests the letters wander into a new order

parts.note: Hyde Park is the famous London park

explanation.surface: An elephant gets cramp walking round a park.
explanation.walkthrough: Hyde Park is the large royal park in central London; 'possibly' marks the elephant as one example of the class.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick-skinned mammal such as a rhino or elephant is the class meant; 'possibly' marks the example.

clue.text: Left decoration in lower part of ear

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, a decoration

explanation.surface: An earring is left as a decoration on the lower ear.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft fleshy part hanging at the bottom of the ear has this anatomical name.

clue.text: Sauce, one originally unknown in South America

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the abbreviation for the continent
originally means the word one gives only its opening letter

parts.note: y is a standard algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A condiment, once unheard of in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Soy sauce is a condiment made from soya beans.

clue.text: Support one by returning call — it's helpful in court

parts.note: a leg supports a table
a means one

indicators.note: the word for call is read backwards

parts.note: to dial is to call on the phone

explanation.surface: Someone backs a friend by returning a call, which helps them in a legal case.
explanation.definitionFit: State-funded assistance for those who cannot pay lawyers is useful in court.

clue.text: Second taxi driver's showing healing scars

parts.note: a cabby drives a taxi

explanation.surface: A second cab driver shows healing wounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Covered in crusts over healing wounds describes skin that is scabbed.

clue.text: Problematic situation, finding way into glue factory?

explanation.surface: A difficult position found while getting into a glue works.
explanation.walkthrough: A wicket is also a small gate, so a sticky one is a fitting way into a glue factory; the question mark flags this play.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricky position (from cricket on a damp pitch); read literally, a gummy small gate, an entrance to an adhesive works.

clue.text: Degree subject?

parts.note: looks like a university course, but the degree is one of temperature, and the subject is measuring it

explanation.surface: A student asks what to study for a degree.
explanation.definitionFit: The science of measuring temperature deals in degrees.

clue.text: Finishing study with cryptic writing about daughter

parts.note: to con is to study

indicators.note: the word for cryptic writing goes about the abbreviation

parts.note: cluing is the writing of cryptic clues

explanation.surface: Someone completes their studies with a coded essay about a daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bringing to an end is finishing.

clue.text: House expert renovated Oslo garret

indicators.note: renovation remakes something, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A property expert does up an attic in Norway's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' suggests property; it is one of the twelve houses of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: Horoscope-casters divide the heavens into twelve houses.

clue.text: River and lake bird

parts.note: the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: A bird on a river and lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is a river in England.
explanation.definitionFit: An old name for the blackbird or the dipper.

clue.text: Garland certainly made to appear casual

parts.note: a lei is a Hawaiian flower garland
surely means certainly

explanation.surface: Wearing a flower garland certainly makes one look relaxed.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhurried and relaxed, as in a slow stroll, is the casual sense.

clue.text: Reformed Hercules accepts nothing lustful

indicators.note: the shuffled letters take in the zero
reformed means formed again, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A reformed hero no longer has lecherous desires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformed' rearranges HERCULES, and 'accepts' puts O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewd and full of desire describes lust.

clue.text: Cunning, entering with long strides, at an angle

indicators.note: the striding word goes inside the word for cunning

parts.note: sly means cunning
loping is running with long easy strides

explanation.surface: A crafty figure strides in at a slant.
explanation.definitionFit: Slanting, on a slope, is at an angle.

clue.text: Chemical spray used on right person carrying club

parts.note: Mace is a brand of irritant spray

explanation.surface: A chemical irritant is used on the right person holding a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' is the ceremonial staff called a mace.
explanation.definitionFit: An official bearing a ceremonial staff in procession carries it.

clue.text: Material supplied by a French gospel song?

parts.note: un is French for a
a spiritual is a religious folk song

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a French gospel song provides the material.
explanation.definitionFit: Worldly, concerned with bodily rather than soul matters, is material.

clue.text: Roman pair calling in a doctor for the feet

indicators.note: the numeral pair calls in, taking inside, the doctor

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals
MB is a medical degree, a doctor

explanation.surface: Two Romans summon a doctor to treat their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Metrical feet, short-long, are the plural of a poetry term.

clue.text: Calm in Scottish island where Liberal replaces leader

indicators.note: the abbreviation for Liberal takes the place of the island's first letter

parts.note: Mull is an island in the Hebrides

explanation.surface: A quiet spell on a Scottish island where a Liberal ousts the chief.
explanation.walkthrough: Mull is an island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiet period or pause is a calm.

clue.text: One lady losing article dashed around vainly

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: dashed about means the remaining letters are thrown into a new order
the word lady drops the article

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A lady loses something and dashes around in vain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes the article out of 'lady' before 'dashed around' shuffles what is left; the surface reads 'dashed' as rushed.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something to no purpose is doing it in vain.

clue.text: Peacekeepers passed on, we hear — it's natural

parts.note: UN peacekeepers belong to the United Nations

indicators.note: the word for died is said aloud as a word for coloured

parts.note: passed on means died

explanation.surface: Peacekeepers who die, it is reported, are only natural.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric left uncoloured keeps its natural shade.

clue.text: Quickly glancing at kim's broken pottery

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: the name Kim with its s gives the letters to shuffle
Ming porcelain is valuable Chinese pottery

explanation.surface: Someone glances quickly at Kim's smashed vases.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading lightly over the surface is glancing quickly.

clue.text: Exotic bays, extremely lovely features along the side of the road

definitions.text: features along the side of the road

indicators.note: exotic means unusual and foreign, so the letters are made strange in a new order
extremely means only the outermost letters of lovely are used

explanation.surface: Exotic bays with lovely roadside views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives L and Y from 'lovely', and 'Exotic' shuffles them with BAYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Parking places beside a road where drivers stop off are lay-bys.

clue.text: Something to tie up ruler — a bit of wood

parts.note: string is used to tie things up
ER is the Queen, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A cord to bind a ruler, a piece of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A long horizontal timber supporting a floor or staircase is this beam.
